battle.name: 乍得內戰 (1998年-2002年)
battle.brief: 中文維基「戰爭列表」所列的乍得內戰 (1998年-2002年) 自1998年4月展開，主要席捲乍得中南部，政府軍與反對派武裝爭奪城鎮及交通通道。以裝備服役年為判準，1998年以前已列裝的美製加特林機槍 (Gatling gun) 亦符合年代條件，屬早期制式連發地面火器。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 加特林機槍是美國陸軍早期制式的連發地面火器，由炮組操作，機關槍化後可提供較高持續火力，主要承擔固定或陣地支援任務，而非單兵輕機槍。

countries: 這場衝突的主要交戰空間是乍得本土：中央政府與效忠伊德里斯·德比·伊特諾的部隊，對抗哈桑·賈馬斯、馬哈馬特·努里、阿杜姆·托伊等不同派系所率領的武裝。法國不是名義上的旁觀者；1998年的「雀鷹行動」及2002年的首都保衛戰，都包含撤離重要人員、空運、武器、情報與空中支援。利比亞在1990年代後期與乍得政府決裂後，原有軍事援助網絡曾支持部分反對派，但援助對象與時間並非固定。中非共和國南部及卡洛、薩赫接壤地帶曾是反對派基地、軍火運輸區與政府軍跨境攻擊的所在。喀麥隆、剛果共和國的邊境與機場構成後勤通道，加彭則承辦了2002年的自由城談判。
countriesEn: The main theatre of this conflict was Chad itself: the central government and forces loyal to Idriss Déby Itno fought armed groups led by Hassan Djamous, Mahamat Nouri, Adoum Togoï, and several other commanders whose organizations did not always act under a single chain of command. France was not merely a nominal observer. Operation Épervier in 1998 and the defence of the capital in 2002 involved the evacuation of important personnel, airlift, weapons, intelligence, and air support. After relations with the Chadian government broke down in the late 1990s, Libya's former military assistance network supported some rebel factions, although the recipients and duration of that aid varied. Southern areas of the Central African Republic and the border zones around Ké and Sarh served as rebel bases, arms-transfer routes, and targets of cross-border government operations. Cameroon and the Republic of Congo provided strategically important border and airport links for logistics, while Gabon hosted the Libreville negotiations of 2002.
people: 伊德里斯·德比·伊特諾自1990年起擔任乍得總統，兼任武裝力量最高指揮者；1998年首都危急時，他依靠法國協助保住政治與軍事指揮中樞。前武裝部隊總司令哈桑·賈馬斯因與德比的政治及軍隊權力衝突成為早期反對派核心，他與追隨其北方網絡的馬哈馬特·努里共同構成1998年軍事挑戰的重要領導層。阿杜姆·托伊則是後來反對派聯盟中「民主與發展運動」的領導人，2002年首都攻勢主要由其政治軍事網絡推動。法國方面，席哈克政府批准並執行秘密援助，法國飛行員、特遣隊、軍事顧問和情報人員分別負責空運、火力、戰術協調及後勤。各 rebel commanders 的目標與資源並不相同，不能把整個反對派視為接受同一位指揮官永久控制的單一軍隊。
peopleEn: Idriss Déby Itno, president of Chad since 1990, also held the highest authority over the armed forces; when the capital was in danger in 1998, French assistance enabled him to preserve the political and military command centre. Hassan Djamous, the former commander-in-chief of the armed forces, became a principal leader of the early opposition after his political and command disputes with Déby. Together with Mahamat Nouri and the northern network that followed him, Djamous helped organize the military challenge of 1998. Adoum Togoï, leader of the Movement for Democracy and Development, was central to the rebel coalition that later mounted the 2002 offensive against the capital. On the French side, the Chirac government authorized and conducted covert assistance through aircrew, special-operations personnel, military advisers, and intelligence officers responsible respectively for airlift, fire support, tactical coordination, and logistics. The rebel commanders did not share identical objectives or resources, and the opposition should not be treated as a single army under one permanent commander.
kits: 可確認的裝備包括政府軍的T-55坦克、BTR-60裝甲運兵車及少量MiG-21系列戰鬥機，另有以四輪驅動車改裝的武裝技術車和Ural-375柴油卡車；步兵主要使用AK-47、AKM、PKM、FN MAG與RPG-7。反對派同樣大量使用蘇聯制式或利比亞庫存的上述步槍、通用機槍與火箭筒，並以皮卡技術車保持機動。法國特遣隊配備FAMAS步槍，法國空軍的Mirage 2000C則是1998年已服役、2002年可投入支援的機型。彈藥供應並不統一：AK系列需7.62×39毫米彈，PKM使用7.62×54毫米彈，技術車上的12.7毫米槍需另一種重彈，T-55依賴125毫米坦克彈，Mirage 2000則有30毫米機炮。不同口徑、備用電池、柴油、輪胎與裝甲車零件的短缺，使空運到首都後仍必須依靠受保護的道路運輸。
kitsEn: Confirmed equipment included the government army's T-55 tanks, BTR-60 armoured personnel carriers, and a small number of MiG-21-series fighters, together with four-wheel-drive technical vehicles and Ural-375 diesel trucks. Infantry on both sides primarily used AK-47 and AKM rifles, PKM and FN MAG machine guns, and RPG-7 launchers. The rebels also drew heavily on Soviet-pattern or Libyan-held weapons of these types and used pickup-based technical vehicles to preserve mobility. French special-operations personnel carried FAMAS rifles, while the French Air Force's Mirage 2000C was already in service in 1998 and available for support in 2002. Ammunition was not standardized: AK-pattern weapons required 7.62×39 mm ammunition, the PKM used 7.62×54 mm, technical-vehicle guns needed a different heavy 12.7 mm cartridge, the T-55 depended on 125 mm tank rounds, and the Mirage 2000 carried a 30 mm cannon. The coexistence of different calibres, together with shortages of batteries, diesel, tyres, and armoured-vehicle spares, meant that supplies arriving by air still had to be moved onward over protected roads.
tactics: 1998年政府軍不追求在廣大北部建立連續正面防線，而優先保住首都的中央電台、政府區、總統警衛及主要空運點；法軍以快速空運帶入精銳突擊隊和補給，再由裝甲步兵封住通往首都的道路。反對派則以多支輕裝車隊沿鄉間道路推進，利用技術車先偵察、破壞路障，再讓步兵進入守軍薄弱的據點；受阻後迅速退回北方廣大地區。1999年北方反攻主要沿阿貝謝—法亞拉若—博爾庫及查德湖走廊展開，政府軍則以固定路障、偵察飛行和由南部運來的機動縱隊切斷其補給。2000年的跨境行動沿薩赫—凱—班巴里方向打擊基地與軍火庫存。2002年反對派聯盟利用夜色和多路滲透，由西北地方道路及阿貝謝—布塞方向逼近首都；政府軍集中預備隊，以T-55限制主要通道，再用法國空中支援、迫擊砲與技術車反擊。反對派未能持續控制市區，撤退後政府軍停止大規模追擊並轉入談判。
tacticsEn: In 1998 the government army did not attempt to hold a continuous front across the vast north. It concentrated on protecting the central radio station, government quarter, presidential guard, and principal airlift point in the capital. French forces rapidly airlifted assault troops and supplies, after which armoured infantry sealed the roads leading toward the capital. The rebels used multiple lightly equipped columns on secondary roads: technical vehicles reconnoitred and attacked roadblocks before infantry entered weakly held posts, and the columns dispersed back into the northern interior when blocked. Their principal 1999 counteroffensive followed the Abéché–Faya-Largeau–Borkou axis and the Lake Chad corridor, while the government used roadblocks, reconnaissance flights, and motorized columns supplied from the south to disrupt their logistics. The cross-border operation of 2000 followed the Sarh–Ké–Bambari direction and struck bases and weapons depots. In April 2002 the rebel coalition used darkness and several penetrations from local roads in the northwest and along the Abéché–Boussé approaches. The government concentrated its reserves, used T-55 tanks to restrict the main avenues, and combined French air support, mortars, and technical vehicles in the counterattack. Unable to maintain continuous control of the urban area, the rebels withdrew, after which the government limited large-scale pursuit and shifted to negotiations.
data: 時間線可分成幾個明確節點：1998年2月中旬，德比與前武裝部隊總司令哈桑·賈馬斯的衝突演變成首都危機，法國隨即展開「雀鷹行動」，協助重要人員撤往布拉柴維爾，並把忠于政府的突擊隊及補給送回；反對派至1998年春夏未能占穩首都，退入博爾庫、恩內迪及查德湖周邊。1999年，北方反對派再以機動縱隊向阿貝謝與查德湖方向推進，但在法方情報、空運與政府軍地面縱隊配合下失去延續作戰的能力。2000年，德比把戰線推過卡洛邊境，沿薩赫—凱—班巴里走廊攻擊反對派基地和軍火集散地。2001年，各派反抗力量加強聯繫，準備從北方與西北方向同時施壓。2002年4月15日夜至18日，聯盟攻入首都西側及政府區邊緣，政府依靠總統警衛、預備隊與外來空中支援將其逐出，Mirage 2000C也曾低空飛越首都；公開資料不足以可靠判定每次機炮射擊的結果。4月下旬後叛軍撤退，8月31日政府與主要反對派在自由城簽署協議。關於1998年及2002年戰鬥的傷亡，各來源數字互相矛盾且缺少可核對名冊，因此不能可靠列出雙方陣亡、受傷或被俘的精確人數。
dataEn: The chronology can be divided into several distinct phases. In mid-February 1998, the dispute between Déby and former armed-forces commander Hassan Djamous developed into a crisis in the capital. France immediately began Operation Épervier, helped evacuate important personnel to Brazzaville, and returned government assault troops and supplies. By the spring and summer of 1998 the opposition had failed to hold the capital and withdrew into the Borkou, Ennedi, and Lake Chad regions. In 1999 the northern rebels again advanced with motorized columns toward Abéché and Lake Chad, but lost the capacity to sustain operations as French intelligence and airlift worked with government ground columns. In 2000 Déby carried the war across the Central African Republic border, striking rebel bases and weapons depots along the Sarh–Ké–Bambari corridor. During 2001 the rebel movements strengthened their contacts and prepared pressure from the north and northwest. From the night of 15 to 18 April 2002, the coalition entered western districts and reached the edge of the government quarter before the presidential guard, government reserves, and foreign air support forced it out. A Mirage 2000C also made low-level passes over the capital; public records are insufficient to determine reliably the result of every cannon pass. The rebels withdrew later in April, and on 31 August the government and principal rebel movements signed an agreement in Libreville. Published casualty figures for the fighting in 1998 and 2002 conflict with one another and lack verifiable rosters, so precise totals for killed, wounded, or captured cannot responsibly be stated.
cause: 衝突的根因不是單一的口號或部族問題，而是國家軍隊整編、指揮權和資源分配長期失衡。德比依賴總統警衛與新組建的政府軍控制國家，前政府軍軍官、地方民兵及北方武裝則保有自己的武器網絡；乍得長期依賴外來援助維持軍隊薪餉和裝備，使誰能取得國家職位、外援與地方資源成為核心爭端。1990年代後期利比亞與乍得決裂，原先用於維持內部平衡的武器、訓練和庇護關係部分轉向反對派，令原本分立的武裝獲得再武裝機會。卡洛與薩赫之間的跨境基地、軍火通道及油運走廊所帶來的權力與收益競爭，又使邊境衝突不斷延伸。1998年，賈馬斯等前軍方核心人物加入反對派並發動軍事挑戰，成為這一輪全面內戰的直接引爆點。
causeEn: The conflict arose not from a single slogan or ethnic division but from long-running imbalances in the integration of the armed forces, the distribution of command authority, and control of resources. Déby relied on the presidential guard and government-controlled units, while former armed-forces officers, local militias, and northern armed groups retained their own weapons networks. Because Chad depended heavily on foreign assistance to pay troops and maintain equipment, control of state office, external patronage, and local resources became a central struggle. After relations with Libya broke down in the late 1990s, weapons, training, and sanctuary relationships previously used to balance Chad's internal politics shifted partly toward the opposition, enabling separated armed groups to rearm. Competition surrounding cross-border bases, arms routes, and the oil corridor between the CAR and Sarh extended the fighting beyond Chad's interior. In 1998 the addition of former senior military figures such as Djamous to the rebellion and their launch of a military challenge became the immediate trigger for this renewed civil war.
impact: 軍事層面的直接結果是政府軍在1998年保住首都，1999至2000年逐步恢復北部道路與跨境補給線的反制能力，並在2002年擊退進入首都的反對派聯盟；但中央政府對廣大邊境地區的控制仍不穩定，首都保衛戰更顯示其防衛高度依賴總統警衛、外來情報與法國空中支援。武器在多次轉手和跨境攻擊中流入不同武裝，留下相當數量的步槍、機槍、火箭筒、軍用卡車及備件，後來的解除武裝、整編和再安置因此更困難。反對派高層由武裝鬥爭轉向談判與政治組織，部分人員進入政府軍或公共體系，另有派系拒絕完整整合，使軍隊與政治反對之間的界線變得模糊。這一階段化解了首都攻勢，卻沒有解決軍隊整編、邊境治理和國家資源分配等結構問題，因而成為乍得更大內戰反覆出現的軍事與政治背景。
impactEn: At the military level, the government preserved the capital in 1998, recovered the ability to contest northern roads and cross-border supply lines during 1999 and 2000, and defeated the coalition that entered the capital in 2002. Its control over the extensive border regions nevertheless remained insecure, while the defence of the capital showed how heavily the government depended on the presidential guard, foreign intelligence, and French air support. Weapons changed hands repeatedly during raids and cross-border operations, leaving substantial quantities of rifles, machine guns, launchers, military trucks, and spare parts across several armed groups. Disarmament, integration, and later reintegration consequently became more difficult. Rebel leaders moved from armed struggle into negotiation and political organization; some entered the government forces or public institutions, while other factions refused complete integration, blurring the boundary between the army and legal political opposition. The phase contained the offensive against the capital but did not resolve armed-forces integration, border governance, or the distribution of national resources, leaving the military and political conditions that repeatedly produced renewed rebellion within Chad's larger civil war.
result: 1998至2002年的階段性結果，是德比政府先在首都保衛戰中擊退哈桑·賈馬斯等早期反對派，又於1999至2000年以封鎖道路、空中與情報協助及跨境攻擊削弱北方反對派；2002年阿杜姆·托伊聯盟試圖奪取首都並迫使政府垮台，也因缺少持續控制市區、補給線及外來支援而失敗。4月下旬起叛軍撤回西方與北方，政府的反擊追擊受到政治與後勤條件限制，雙方遂以談判取代立即全面決戰。2002年8月31日的自由城協議規定停火、赦免、解除武裝與武裝人員整編，並為國際監督的解除武裝、解除後收容和重建程序建立框架；實際執行分批進行且並不完全一致。此一協議沒有消滅所有武裝或終止更廣泛的乍得衝突，部分未納入機制的人日後再起，但1998至2002年的主要軍事對抗至此由公開內戰轉為不穩定停火與有限整編。
resultEn: The outcome of the 1998–2002 phase was that Déby's government first repelled the early opposition associated with Hassan Djamous, then used road interdiction, air and intelligence assistance, and cross-border operations to weaken the northern rebel formations during 1999 and 2000. The coalition led politically by Adoum Togoï attempted to seize the capital in 2002 and force the collapse of the government, but it failed because it could not maintain continuous control of the urban area, secure its supply lines, or obtain equivalent foreign support. From late April the rebels withdrew toward the west and north, and the government's pursuit was limited by political and logistical constraints, allowing negotiations to replace immediate all-out combat. The Libreville Agreement of 31 August 2002 provided for a ceasefire, amnesty, disarmament, and the integration of armed personnel, while establishing a framework for internationally supported disarmament, reintegration, and reconstruction. Implementation was phased and uneven. The accord did not eliminate every armed group or end the broader Chadian conflict, and some people excluded from the process later returned to violence, but the principal military confrontation of 1998–2002 gave way to an unstable ceasefire and a limited integration process.
